$comment: ★★★ RIP-RELATIVE ADDRESSING — `leaq msg(%rip), %rax`, the spelling gcc -S writes for every global access (P68 round 9, D-ASM-RIP-RELATIVE-SPELLING-NEEDS-AN-IP-REGISTER). ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23 at the round-9 base: every `sym(%rip)` form was refused ('a symbol-relative memory operand needs a relocation this build does not reach from assembly yet'), a numeric one failed at `unknown register 'rip'`, and `table+16` did not parse. gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 run this file to 42 (ELF, -no-pie and -pie). What each shape proves, by the exit code: `(%rip)` is the address of the NEXT instruction and `-7(%rip)` from a 7-byte lea the lea itself (both compared with the label there, so a mod=10 RBP encoding or a displacement taken from the wrong end fails); `movl $5, counter(%rip)` has 4 immediate bytes AFTER its displacement, so a relocation that ignored them would store 4 bytes past `counter`; `table+16` and `tail-8` name one word, so an addend dropped or a `-8` read as the number -8 fails; `leaq 1f(%rip)` + `jmp *%rdi` branches through an interior label's address. The Mach-O arm RUNS only on the darwin leg (not measured by this lane); its object-file relocations were measured against clang's (X86_64_RELOC_SIGNED / SIGNED_1 / SIGNED_2 / SIGNED_4 with the addend in place) and the reader's decode of them is pinned in `tests/link/test_input_section_units.cpp`. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE: remove `pcRelativeMemoryBase` from the target and every line is refused; drop the walker's bytes-after-field reduction and the store lands 4 bytes off (exit differs). The `release` arm pins only that naming the release pipeline does not break the assembly path.
